raw_response:
Let me think this through as the farmer I am.

---

I'm 69, been working these 7 mu since I was a young man. My wife helps me, and our son sends money from the city but comes back for the busy times — wheat harvest in June, maize harvest in September-October. So really it's the two of us most days, and I'm not as strong as I used to be. That matters for how I plan.

The wheat-maize rotation is what we've always done here in Quzhou. I won't change that. My land is decent — not the best, not the worst. Flat, irrigated from the tube well the village shares. Water costs real money now because the electricity for pumping keeps going up, so I try not to irrigate more than I need to.

**Winter wheat (already in the ground this past October, but planning how I finish it):**

I planted in mid-October like always, used the "Jimai 22" variety seed I bought from the agro shop — good winter-hardy variety, about 15 yuan/mu for seed. Before planting I broadcast compound fertilizer (15-15-15), about 40 kg/mu, and plowed it in. That gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K up front.

In spring at jointing (around late March), I'll topdress urea — about 20 kg/mu of urea, which gives another 9 kg N. So total nitrogen around 15 kg/mu. The extension guy keeps telling us 18 is better but I've been doing 15 for years and getting 400+ kg/mu, so why change. If I see the wheat looking pale I might add a bit more.

Irrigation: one winter watering in December if the ground is dry, then at jointing, then at grain-filling. Usually 3 times. If it rains well in spring I skip one.

Spray herbicide once in early spring for the broadleaf weeds, and one fungicide/insecticide mix around heading time for aphids and powdery mildew. That's the usual routine.

Expect around 430 kg/mu — that's been my average the last few years.

**Summer maize (plant in June right after wheat harvest):**

No time to waste between wheat and maize — I use the no-till planter that our village co-op rents out, about 30 yuan/mu including driver. Drill the maize right into the wheat stubble within 3-4 days of combining. "Zhengdan 958" seed usually, around 25 yuan/mu.

I put compound fertilizer down with the planter, about 30 kg/mu of 15-15-15. Then topdress urea at V8-V10 stage (around late July), 25 kg/mu. Total N about 16 kg/mu. For maize I actually lean a bit higher than wheat because the yield response is good.

Irrigation: usually 1-2 times for maize — once if it's dry around tasseling, and maybe once earlier if June is hot and dry. Summer rains usually help.

One herbicide spray after planting. Sometimes a spray for corn borer if I see it.

Expect around 480 kg/mu. Had a good year in 2024, bad year in 2023 when it was too wet at harvest.

**Labor and cash:**

At my age I can't do heavy work like I used to. I pay for the combine harvester at wheat and maize time (about 50 yuan/mu each), and the no-till planter for maize. Spraying and fertilizer I still do myself with a knapsack sprayer. My wife helps with everything except the heavy lifting.

Cash is always tight before harvest. I buy fertilizer on short credit from the shop in town — pay when the wheat is sold.
